description: First-pass machine-readable rules for mapping Phase 3 and Phase 4 signatures to H0/H1/H2 hypothesis states.

audit_ready.description: All minimum coverage checks needed for a hypothesis audit are satisfied.

m0_balanced_strata.description: Pass, fail, and control strata are all present in the candidate set.

m0_matched_set_count.description: Number of pass/fail/control matched audit sets carried forward into causal testing.

m1_semantic_role_accuracy.description: Leave-one-out centroid accuracy for semantic-role probes at the traced layer.

m1_surface_control_gap.description: Semantic-role accuracy minus surface-position accuracy; negative values mean surface cues are easier to decode.

m1_filler_gap.description: Within-vs-between cosine gap for filler identity stability.

m1_predicate_gap.description: Within-vs-between cosine gap for predicate identity stability.

m2_joint_success_rate.description: Rate at which interchange both transfers donor filler identity and preserves the target role.

m2_role_preservation_rate.description: Rate at which role readout survives structure-preserving interchange.

m2_donor_transfer_rate.description: Rate at which donor filler identity transfers under interchange.

m3_selective_impairment.description: Semantic-role impairment beyond predicate-control impairment under targeted ablation.

m4_rescue_rate.description: Rate at which donor patching rescues an incorrect fail-item role readout.

m5_fail_item_rescue_coverage.description: Fraction of fail candidates that exhibit at least one rescue signal in item-level linkage.

audit_preconditions.description: Phase 3 and Phase 4 provide enough coverage to support an H0/H1/H2 audit.
The run contains enough matched audit sets for causal comparisons.

hypotheses.label: Binding hypothesis
hypotheses.description: Role-filler binding is a primary mechanism for systematic behaviour.

states.meaning: Claimed binding structure exists and is causally used.

all.description: A role-carrying representation is decodable above a minimal floor.
Interchange preserves target roles at a strong rate.
Interchange transfers donor filler identity at a non-trivial rate.
Targeted ablation selectively impairs semantic-role readout.
Binding-compatible patching rescues fail items at a meaningful rate.
Rescue is distributed across enough fail items to matter.

states.meaning: Claimed binding structure exists but is not effectively used.

all.description: Filler identity remains at least moderately stable.
Targeted ablation still shows some selective semantic damage.

any.description: Interchange preserves the role even if donor transfer is weak.
Failure rescue exists but remains sparse.
Some fail items do show rescue-linked evidence.

states.meaning: Claimed binding structure is absent or behaviourally irrelevant.

hypotheses.label: Distributed geometry hypothesis
hypotheses.description: Systematicity is carried by distributed subspaces or stable geometry.

states.meaning: Stable geometry exists and is causally used for behaviour.

all.description: Targeted ablation causes selective semantic impairment.

any.description: Geometry-aware patching recovers some incorrect items.
Rescue evidence generalizes to a non-trivial subset of fail items.

states.meaning: Stable geometry exists but is weakly or inconsistently used.

any.description: Filler geometry is at least somewhat stable.
Predicate geometry is at least somewhat stable.

none.description: There is essentially no causal effect under targeted ablation.

states.meaning: No stable geometry relevant to behaviour is present.

hypotheses.label: Shortcut hypothesis
hypotheses.description: Behaviour is mostly supported by surface heuristics or direct routes.

states.meaning: Shortcut route is the dominant mechanism behind behaviour.

all.description: Surface cues are easier to decode than semantic roles.
Structure-preserving interchange rarely succeeds end to end.

any.description: Donor transfer remains weak under interchange.
Rescue signals cover only a minority of fail items.

states.meaning: Shortcut signals exist but are not dominant.

all.description: Surface cues are at least competitive with semantic-role signals.
